summary: The cumulative installer can claim ownership of bytes it never wrote and can write a manifest after aborting before any apply step.

blockers.defect: An existing file whose bytes match the shipped file is recorded as installer-owned even if the installer never wrote it. A later update or removal can then destroy that file without a backup.
blockers.evidence: scripts/install-team-config.ts:276-280 adds the hash to both the next and partial manifests and skips the write when bytes match; lines 282-284 and 299-305 choose no backup when the current hash matches the previous manifest. For example, a pre-existing AGENTS.md identical to the initial source is adopted on first install; after the source changes, its original bytes are replaced without backup. This violates the invariant that content the installer did not write is never lost.
blockers.change: Track actual ownership separately from content equality, or preserve the pre-existing file before claiming it; add a regression covering an identical pre-existing file followed by an update and removal.

blockers.defect: An apply-time containment or state failure before the first successful step still creates or replaces the manifest, despite no step having been applied.
blockers.evidence: scripts/install-team-config.ts:344 verifies the first step, but any failure enters the unconditional partial-manifest write at lines 374-377. On a fresh agent directory, changing a planned parent into a symlink in beforeApply causes verify to reject and nevertheless creates .team-config-manifest.json. Fix entry 2 requires an abort before changing anything on the first symlink component; entry 9 describes a partial manifest for steps already applied.
blockers.change: Only persist a partial manifest when an actual managed mutation requiring a manifest update has succeeded; add a fresh-directory apply-time symlink test that checks the entire agent directory, including manifest absence.
